case_study_packaging.headline: PE-backed addiction treatment network captures $412K in annual savings and a 22% EMR fee cut in just six months
case_study_packaging.client_problem_statement: Rapid expansion left SaVida Health with a patchwork of vendors, location-by-location purchasing, and minimal spend visibility across its 20+ outpatient medication-assisted treatment clinics. With private-equity owner Council Capital targeting near-term EBITDA lift, leadership needed a fast, low-disruption way to trim indirect costs while safeguarding clinical operations and growth plans.
approach_summary: Analyzed $5.3 million in indirect spend across 10 categories to target the highest-value opportunities first.
Renegotiated the incumbent Athena EMR contract, dropping fees from 4.56% to 3.40% of collections and securing $358K in hard annual savings.
Enrolled SaVida in the Provista GPO, unlocking 10–34% discounts on high-use medical and office-supply SKUs and standardizing purchasing through existing Staples and Henry Schein channels.
Consolidated fragmented Comcast Business circuits under a single managed-services agreement and rationalized bandwidth to release 15-20% telecom savings potential.
Created centralized spend dashboards and a SharePoint contract repository to institutionalize data-driven sourcing going forward.
top_levers: Competitive benchmarking / alternate VAR quoting (IT hardware)
case_study_packaging.value_delivered_blurb: Treya delivered $412,065 in identified annual run-rate savings—almost double the $210K minimum guarantee—with $357,889 already contracted within 196 days of kickoff. The engagement provides more than a 2.3× return on Treya’s $175K fixed fee while equipping SaVida with a GPO platform, consolidated telecom roadmap, and a repeatable strategic sourcing playbook.
where_we_were_unique: Achieved first hard savings inside six months by sequencing a high-impact EMR renegotiation.
Leveraged deep healthcare GPO expertise to secure Provista pricing that SaVida could access without changing day-to-day ordering workflows.
Hands-on data collection directly from suppliers overcame the client’s limited internal spend visibility.
Collaborative, low-disruption approach safeguarded clinical operations and maintained strong incumbent supplier relationships.
